title: Temujin and Jamukha, Sworn Brothers
text:
The Secret History of the Mongols, written in the 13th century, tells how the boy Temujin, later Genghis Khan, met another boy, Jamukha, on the frozen Onon River. They became anda, sworn brothers, exchanging knucklebones for playing games and later arrowheads. As young men they renewed the oath.

When Temujin's wife Borte was kidnapped by the Merkits, Jamukha joined the war that rescued her. Afterward the two camped together for about a year and a half and were inseparable. Then one day, as the camp moved, Jamukha said something ambiguous about where they should pitch their tents. Temujin, on Borte's advice, read it as a sign that Jamukha wanted him under his command, and he moved on through the night. Many followers came with him.

The friends became rivals for leadership of the steppe. Jamukha was proclaimed gurkhan by a coalition and fought Temujin for years. In 1205, defeated and on the run, he was betrayed by his own companions, who handed him over. Temujin had the traitors executed for betraying their lord. According to the Secret History, he offered Jamukha friendship again. Jamukha refused, saying that he would only trouble Temujin like a louse in his collar or a thorn in his lapel, and asked to be put to death without shedding his blood. Temujin granted his request.
lesson: Friendships need shared aims to survive ambition. When paths split, part honestly, because rivalry between old friends can become the hardest kind.
source: The Secret History of the Mongols, chapters 3 to 8
caveat: The Secret History mixes history with literary storytelling, and Jamukha's last speech in particular may be shaped by the author.
